tr_definition: TOFU Eq. 1 (arithmetic mean over perturbed), per-fact mean over 40
crossing_rule: first crossing of mean_tr >= level; every crossing logged
mu_rule: a level checkpoint with model_utility_6 below mu_threshold is excluded
fact_set: all 40 facts; facts 8 and 22 fail the ceiling check and are REPORTED, not dropped, from the mean that drives level crossings
forget_quality_primary: two-sided KS vs fr_retain (TOFU). At n=m=40 its achievable p-values are a ~6-step ladder from our starting point to 1.0; show the ladder, never read one step as a finding
forget_quality_secondary: none. No test outside TOFU/Farashah/Xiang is added; the coarseness above is reported as a limitation, not patched with a statistic of our own
stage1_gate3: FAILED as written: KS p = 0.0286, need < 0.01. Diagnosis: D = 0.325 = 13/40, and p < 0.01 needs 14/40 -- one fact's worth of separation. Injection itself is unambiguous fact by fact, P(gold) higher on 40/40, NLI on 39/40, truth ratio lower on 33/40. Recorded, not rescued.
stage3_depth_rule: Match on ACHIEVED truth ratio, not the level label. A level is a trigger: the probe runs every 2 optimizer steps (= 1 epoch at 40 forget examples / effective batch 32), so each language overshoots its trigger by however far it moved in that epoch (ja +0.006, id +0.085). Per language take the crossing whose achieved mean_tr_norm is nearest a common target T, sweeping T for the deepest choice that stays tight. T = 0.833 gives max deviation 0.014 across en/id/ja/ru.
stage3_deviation_from_stage2: Stage 2 pre-registered ONE shared nominal level for all languages. Matching on the label gives achieved TR 0.834-0.913 (spread 0.079); matching on the achieved value gives 0.819-0.847 (spread 0.028). The rule above reads ONLY the truth ratio -- the pre-registered matching variable -- and never P(gold), NLI or MU, so it is not selection on an outcome-adjacent quantity. Recorded here BEFORE any relearning is run. The uniform-0.828 numbers are reported alongside in every table.
stage3_french_arm: French is NOT a matched cell and is labelled separately in every figure. Its nearest crossing to T is 0.045 away (3x the worst of the others) because it produced only three distinct checkpoints, and its P(gold) 0.075 sits BELOW the never-taught fr_retain floor of 0.094. It is the same-language reference arm.

stage3_relearn.grid: 5 unlearn languages x 5 relearn languages = 25 cells
stage3_relearn.data: retain99 in the relearn language (BENIGN: different authors, never the forgotten fact)
stage3_relearn.epochs_rationale: a trajectory, not a single point: three points are what distinguish a rising curve from a flat one, which is the direct test of H_attractor (saturation). Dropped the earlier plan of matching the old study's ep2 -- that comparison was already weak (different learn language, probe language, depth and metric variant), and what transfers from that study is structural, not its absolute 42.5%.
stage3_relearn.probe: always French. TWO phrasings: p0 canonical (what LEARN trained on) and p1 = TOFU's own paraphrased_question, as translated by Farashah. p1 separates 'the fact came back' from 'the trained wording came back'.
stage3_relearn.epochs_scored: 1, 2, 3 -- weights-only snapshots from ONE run, not three runs
stage3_relearn.lr_caveat: all epochs share ONE linear schedule (warmup_ratio 0.2, decaying to 0 at the last step), so epochs 1-2 sit at a non-zero LR and epoch 3 is the only annealed point. A flattening between epochs 2 and 3 may be the schedule, not saturation -- plot the LR alongside. The schedule is IDENTICAL in all 25 cells, so it cancels in every cross-cell comparison, which is the only comparison this study makes.
stage3_relearn.p1_confound: on 15 of 40 facts the published p1 question spells the surname differently from p0. p1 is scored AS PUBLISHED and its question text is stored per fact, so matched and mismatched facts can be split at analysis time. Surname normalization is applied only to truth-ratio answers, never to questions.
stage3_relearn.weights_retained: none. 25 cells x 3 epochs x 16GB = 1.2TB against a 500GB limit. Every snapshot is scored then deleted; the per-epoch JSON stores components (not summaries) so every planned metric stays recomputable without a model: TR under both definitions and both surname variants, P(gold), all six NLI class probabilities, generations to 2000 chars, output language, Model Utility AND its 617 per-record values, at both phrasings. Hidden states (Part B) and unprobed phrasings are the only things lost; one cell regenerates in ~3h at the fixed seed.

stage3_primary_outcome: recovery = (TR_unlearned - TR_relearned) / (TR_unlearned - TR_learned) on the surname-normalized TOFU Eq. 1 truth ratio, TR_learned = fr_ft 0.6054. P(gold) and NLI recovery reported on the same definition alongside; none of the three is a tiebreak for the others.
stage3_covariate: each cell's starting P(gold) is reported in every table. The four cross-lingual arms span 0.335-0.492 and French -0.032 of the learned span, so they do NOT start from the same knowledge state; the claim 'all five started equal' is not made.

stage3_hypotheses.H1_depth: recovery is governed by how much the unlearning actually removed, which depends on the UNLEARNING language. Predicts a large row effect ordered by starting P(gold) (en ~ id > ja > ru >> fr), with French near zero.
stage3_hypotheses.H_attractor: the old study's fitted attractor (dTR = 0.800*TR_unl - 0.474, R2 0.868) is the whole story. Pushed through our matched checkpoints it predicts 84-85% recovery in EVERY cell including French, with no row and no column effect.
stage3_hypotheses.H_column: relearn language has no detectable effect, replicating the old study's FACT 96.8% / LANGUAGE 0.0% variance decomposition. Expected to be a null we cannot resolve: the between-language question needs ~2250 facts and forget01 gives 40.
stage3_hypotheses.H_diagonal: relearning in the SAME language the unlearning used shows no excess over off-diagonal cells. Newly askable only because this design varies the unlearn language; the old study fixed it to English.
stage3_hypotheses.discriminating_cell: French. H1 predicts near-zero recovery there, H_attractor predicts 84%.

stage3_power: the power lives in the ROWS, not the columns. The unlearn-language effect is already visible in Stage 2 at a 6x margin on P(gold); the relearn-language effect carries the old study's 126-139pp per-language CIs against an 18-24pp spread and is reported as a replication of an underpowered null, not as a headline.
stage3_secondary_tests: none. As in Stage 1, no test outside TOFU / Farashah / Xiang is added; limitations are reported as limitations.
stage3_held_not_precommitted: a uniform-level-0.828 relearn arm (id@0.828, ru@0.828 kept on disk for it). Run ONLY if recovery turns out to track starting P(gold), and declared post-hoc if so.
stage3_known_limitations: single seed: relearn.py hardcodes set_seed(cfg['seed']) with no --seed flag
content control (retain vs real_authors vs world_facts) still unrun; carried over from the old study as an open item, not a blocker
40 facts = 40 attributes of 2 entities (Basil Mahfouz Al-Kuwaiti 0-19, Nikolai Abilov 20-39); fact-level resampling overstates n
intermediate epochs are mid-LR-schedule, so they are comparable across cells but not to an independently-run shorter job
the fr relearn column re-exposes rows LEARN trained on -- see stage3_relearn_data_confound
NLI partly tracks output language -- see stage3_nli_generation_confound
facts 8 and 22 carry ~11pp of every recovery number -- see stage3_fact_sensitivity
p1 has no learned/unlearned baseline -- see stage3_p1_baseline_gap
stage3_run_record: 2026-09-16. Five row jobs (846886-90) on gpu-long/a100-80. fr, ja, ru completed all 5 cells (~10h each, ~2h per cell). id (846887) and en (846890) FAILED mid-row with nvmlInit_v2 'Driver/library version mismatch' -> NCCL ncclSystemError at torch.distributed.init_process_group: the node driver went out of sync with userspace while the job ran, so the cell in flight finished normally and the NEXT deepspeed launch died before any optimizer step. set -euo pipefail then ended the row. 21/25 cells; en->{id,ja,ru} and id->ru never started and wrote nothing, so no result is partial. Resubmitted as single-cell jobs. NOT a storage or walltime failure (195G of 500G used; completed rows took 10h of a 16h wall). CLOSED 2026-09-17: the four missing cells were rerun on the h100-96 pool (xgpi2, xgpi10) after the driver fault spread to xgph4/6/7/9 -- half the a100-80 pool -- and kept vacuuming up jobs because broken nodes fail instantly and are therefore always idle. Grid is 25/25 cells x 3 epochs = 75 result files, all parsed, all n=40, all per-fact/p1/utility arrays present, no out-of-range values. A cell costs ~1h on h100 against ~2h on a100-80.
stage3_relearn_data_confound: DISCOVERED AT ANALYSIS, NOT PRE-REGISTERED. The fr RELEARN column is not novel data. 01_learn_fr.sbatch trained fr_ft on retain99_fr + forget01_fr (4000 rows), so relearning on retain99 IN FRENCH re-exposes the model to rows it already memorised, while en/id/ja/ru retain99 are genuinely unseen. Evidence: first-step training loss ~0.018 on French relearn data (ulen->fr) against ~2.83 on Japanese (ulid->ja), and final loss 0.015 vs 0.46. The fr column is therefore a different intervention -- re-exposure at ~100x smaller gradients -- and is marked as such in every figure and table. SCOPE: it affects H_column and the fr->fr diagonal cell. It does NOT affect the row comparison, because every row sees the same five columns. Recomputed without the fr column nothing flips: ep3 column spread stays 19.8pp and H_diagonal stays null (56.7% diagonal vs 61.7% off-diagonal). The OLD English study carried the identical asymmetry on its English relearn column, so this is inherited from the design rather than new. Reported as a limitation; no statistic of our own is added to adjust for it.
stage3_nli_generation_confound: NLI is scored on GENERATED text, so it also moves with output language. By relearn language at ep3: en 90% French output / NLI 0.154; fr 98% / 0.305; id 98% / 0.239; ja 98% / 0.232; ru 99% / 0.241. r(French share, NLI) = +0.27 over the 21 cells. Part of the low NLI in the en column is the model answering in the wrong language. Truth ratio and P(gold) are forced-sequence scores and are not exposed to this.
stage3_fact_sensitivity: Facts 8 and 22 fail the Stage 1 ceiling check and the plan says REPORT, not drop. Excluding them at ep3 shifts every cell by a mean -10.8pp (max -21.9pp, id->id 44.0% -> 22.2%), moving the grand mean from ~60% to ~49%. The STRUCTURE is unchanged: ja remains the highest row (80.6%), en the lowest (15.7%), H_diagonal stays null. Both readings are printed in every cell of panel A and the fact set is a --facts flag, not a second script. Leave-one-fact-out at ep3 moves a cell by 6pp (ja->fr) to 36pp (fr->id, driven by fact 6). NO per-fact truth ratio anywhere in the 63 cell-epochs exceeds 3.0, so the old study's fact-14 denominator collapse does NOT recur here.
stage3_p1_baseline_gap: OPEN. measure_fr.py gained the p1 probe after Stages 1 and 2 had already run, so p1 exists only on relearned checkpoints. The pre-registered 'fact vs trained wording' reading needs a difference-in-differences against the learned and unlearned checkpoints, which cannot be computed until fr_ft, fr_retain and the five matched checkpoints are rescored (pure inference, ~1h, weights still on disk). Absolute p1 values at ep3 are reassuring but not a DiD: p1 truth ratio sits +0.016 ABOVE p0 on average (slightly more forgotten, so recovery is not merely the trained wording returning) and p1/p0 P(gold) = 0.68.
